summary.tldr: Lowers the voting age to 16 for federal elections and referendums, and updates related election rules.
what_it_does: Sets the voting age for federal elections at 16 or older on polling day for Canadian citizens.
Applies the same 16-plus voting rule to referendums under the adapted Canada Elections Act.
Changes the definition of “future elector” to mean a Canadian citizen who is 14 or 15 years old.
Removes the rule that election officers appointed under section 32 may be under 18 but must be at least 16.
Updates voting offences, solemn declaration forms, and fundraising disclosure rules to match the new 16-year-old voting age.
summary.background: Under the current Canada Elections Act, a person must be a Canadian citizen and at least 18 years old on polling day to vote. The bill also changes the related referendum regulation to match the new voting age.
